tower.bags.title: Its bags
tower.bags.lede: The closed bags waiting here for a driver. Offer one to a driver who could take it now: they are told, and the notice opens their offer. “Not now”, or no answer in 20 minutes, passes it to the next nearest driver by itself. With nobody left, it is offered again every hour; after a day, the people of its parcels are told it is held up, and told again when it is on the road.
tower.bags.none: No closed bag is waiting here now.
tower.bags.coming: a driver is coming for it
tower.bags.noDrivers: No working driver an offer could reach now: none near with room, within their hours.

tower.messages.lede: What people wrote from the help’s “Write to us”, sorted by what it is about. Safety comes first, then whoever has waited longest. An answer goes by email to the address they gave.

tower.zones.lede: Your country’s zones: each a group of its official areas, each in one of your price groups. Shops and hubs take the zone their pin lies in. Prices by zone come with your price card.

tower.zones.groups.lede: Every zone is in one group, and prices will be set for each group. Name them in your own words. A group a zone still uses cannot be taken away.

tower.density.title: Where hubs are needed
tower.hubList.title: The hub list
tower.hubList.lede: Every hub place in this country: the hubs it has, the places the map says a hub is needed, and the places you add. Fill in a row as you find a hub, move it to negotiating, and send the invitation from it — the hub sign-up with the place and the row’s code. When the hub signs up with it, the row turns joined by itself. A row rejected comes back open after 90 days, or sooner if its numbers double.
tower.hubList.unnamed: A place without a name yet
tower.hubList.stale: The map no longer suggests this place; kept as you left it.
tower.hubList.f.name: Name
tower.density.lede: Each zone by how far its shops are from a hub, judged by its group, or by its parcels; the hubs, the roads between them and how full they run; and what the map suggests, each with its reason. It suggests; you decide. It never approves, moves or closes a hub.
tower.density.noZones: This country has no zones in force yet: publish them on the Zones screen to see coverage and demand by zone.
tower.density.keyCoverage: Green: its shops are within reach of a hub — urban {urban} km, rural {rural} km, remote {remote} km by road. Amber: within twice that. Red: farther. Navy dots: hubs (hollow: local only; red: down). Orange rings: where a hub is suggested.
tower.density.keyDemand: Deeper blue: more parcels handed in and collected there in the last 30 days.
tower.density.areaLabel: {area} — {zone}: {shops, plural, one {# shop} other {# shops}}, {parcels, plural, one {# parcel} other {# parcels}} in 30 days, {km} km from a hub ({coverage})

tower.density.line.extra_hub_ratio: {hub} ran full on {full} of the last {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, and its zones send {ratio} times what it says it sorts a day. Placed in its busiest far zone, {zone}.

tower.density.reachLede: How far by road a zone’s shops may be from a hub, by the zone’s group. This country starts at urban {urban} km, rural {rural} km, remote {remote} km.
tower.catchments.title: Which hubs serve each zone
tower.catchments.hint: {hubs, plural, one {# hub} other {# hubs}} · {unserved, plural, =0 {every zone served} one {# zone without a hub} other {# zones without a hub}}
tower.catchments.lede: A net of hubs: every approved hub serves the zone it stands in by itself, a hub may add neighbouring zones from its own app, and you add a hub to a zone or take one away — the zone it stands in too. A parcel goes to the nearest of its zone’s hubs to its shop that has room on its floor. A zone without a hub is routed as before, by the area name its shops typed; a zone merged or split since keeps the hubs added to the zone it was made from until it has its own.

tower.prices.title: Prices
tower.prices.lede: Your country’s price card: what a parcel costs between two of your zones, by how far apart they are and what it weighs, with a charge for each group’s ends and your surcharges. The two shops’ own fees, our fee and the tax are added to it, as today. A card is approved by a second person and is in force from a date at least your notice ahead. Until a card is in force, prices are worked out as before.
tower.prices.inForce: Card {version} is in force, since {date} (approved by {who}).
tower.prices.noneInForce: No card is in force: prices are worked out as before.

tower.rates.big.title: Large senders’ own rates
tower.rates.big.hint: {n, plural, =0 {None yet} one {# sender with its own rate} other {# senders with their own rate}}
tower.rates.big.about: Your decision (12 November): large senders negotiate. On a fixed card a sender gets its own contract card — a price for each size; by factors, a discount off the formula. One member of staff proposes it, a second approves it; only then does it price that sender’s parcels. Hubs and shops are paid their own fees as before.
